_note: FILL-RULE RESOLUTION and the FLATTENING law. A fill asks one question — is this point inside? — and the two answers differ wherever a path crosses itself, which is exactly where three rasterisers drift. THE LAW: every curve flattens to 16 uniform-parameter line segments (the pinned constant CANVAS_FLATTEN_SEGMENTS; uniform in t, never adaptive, because adaptive subdivision is per-implementation and would make this corpus unpinnable), every subpath is treated as CLOSED for filling, and the crossing test is HALF-OPEN in y: an edge counts when y0 ≤ py < y1 (upward, +1) or y1 ≤ py < y0 (downward, −1), and only when the crossing lies strictly right of the point. `nonzero` fills where the winding number is ≠ 0; `evenodd` fills where the crossing count is odd. `area` is the signed shoelace area of the flattened path — positive is clockwise in the y-down canvas space — and it pins the flattening itself, not just the verdicts. Expected values come from an independent scratch implementation.

cases.name: a pentagram: nonzero fills the core, evenodd punches it out
two subpaths wound the SAME way: nonzero keeps the hole filled
two subpaths wound the OTHER way: both rules punch the hole
an unclosed subpath is implicitly closed for filling
the half-open crossing rule: the top edge is IN, the bottom edge is OUT
